---
title: "Install OS"
---

Use this checklist for a new workstation before running the full lab software setup.

::: {.callout-important title="Supported platform"}
The repository is tested/supported on **Fedora Workstation 44 x86_64**. Install
that edition, major version, and architecture; the main playbook fails its
preflight check before making changes on any other platform.
:::

## 1. Install Fedora Workstation

- Download the Fedora Workstation 44 x86_64 installation image from the [official Fedora website](https://fedoraproject.org/workstation/download/).
- Install it with the default GNOME desktop unless you have a documented reason to do otherwise.
- Apply the first system update offered by GNOME Software or `dnf` before installing the lab stack.

## 2. Clone the repository and install the workstation

Clone the workstation setup repository over HTTPS, enter it, and run the canonical setup command:

```sh
git clone https://github.com/fs-ise/workstation-setup.git
cd workstation-setup
make install
```

`make install` installs the Ansible and Python bootstrap packages, installs the
pinned Ansible Galaxy collections, and runs the workstation playbook. You do
not need to install Ansible separately.

## 3. Verify the inventory

The repository includes the local Ansible `inventory` used by the documented commands. It tells Ansible to configure the current machine. If a workstation needs host-specific variables, create `host_vars/localhost.yml` separately and do not put secrets in it.

::: {.callout-check}
**✅ Check**

```sh
test -f inventory
ansible-inventory -i inventory --list
```
:::

## Optional: Enable SSH if remote administration is needed

Most local workstation setup does not require an SSH server. Enable it only when this machine must be administered remotely:

```sh
sudo systemctl enable --now sshd
systemctl status sshd --no-pager
```
